title: Course Review
description: The closing wrap-up of HTML, CSS & JS: two cumulative review pages that retrieve and apply every module in new scenarios, followed by the course's graded multiple-choice assessment html-css-js/assessments/web-client-mcq.
sourceCoverageNotes: Learner-facing label: every course ends with a module titled exactly 'Course Review'; this module is the HTML, CSS & JS instance, with the course-scoped id html-css-js-course-review.

Inventory of mixed teaching/review modules: none. No HTML, CSS & JS module contains a review topic, the intake records that the slice has no review row and no module check, and all 29 canonical topics are teaching topics (25 core, 1 Reading, 3 S27 Project-day core). Nothing is moved, regrouped or re-pathed.

Both topics here are new Course Review assets, not syllabus rows: each maps no curriculum pointer and adds nothing to the 243-topic canonical count. html-css-js-review-page-and-language reviews html-and-css and javascript-fundamentals; html-css-js-review-browser-client reviews dom-tooling-and-async and fetch-and-browser-client. Every concept they use is taught earlier and listed in their topic.json prerequisites; the few joining details they state (a form button submits and so triggers validation, width: 100% fills the grid column, an async body runs until its first await) are taught on the page before use.

Order at the course end: the four taught modules, then this Course Review module (its two pages in order), then the distinct course-level graded multiple-choice assessment html-css-js/assessments/web-client-mcq listed in course.json assessments. Course Review pages are ungraded practice and carry no GIFT. The former graded practical web-client-practical was retired (user decision, 2026-11-20).
Time fit and the final MCQ's value-free coverage map are recorded in authoring/evidence/html-css-js/course-review-and-final-mcq.md.
